files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.AnimateHumanoid
files.Summary: Animates a humanoid character's walk, run and idle entirely from settings, with no animation clips and no Animator Controller. Add this one component to a character that has a Humanoid Avatar; everything else is configured through its Inspector.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.GaitPose.ArmAngles
files.Summary: Rotational description of one arm, in degrees.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.GaitPose.LegAngles
files.Summary: Rotational description of one leg, in degrees. Amplitudes are derived from the same normalised step length that produces , so the two forms describe the same intended motion.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.GaitPose.LimbTarget
files.Summary: Target for one extremity, for the IK-target space.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.GaitPose.SegmentPose
files.Summary: Position and rotation of a body segment.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.GaitPose
files.Summary: One evaluated frame of gait, expressed in two forms at once so that all three candidate driver spaces of the P2 spike can consume the same source parameters.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.AsymmetryGroup.Side
files.Summary: Which leg 's multipliers apply to.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.AsymmetryGroup
files.Summary: L19 (limp / asymmetric gait): per-leg divergence for one selected leg, applied in WalkGait.EvaluateLeg. The pelvis and torso response (favouring the good leg, rolling onto it, winding up against it) is not authored here — it already falls out of WalkGait.Evaluate's existing leg-differential and weight-balance terms once the two legs' strides diverge, since those derive from leg state rather than from independent oscillators.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.ClipLayeringGroup.BasePoseSource
files.Summary: Which pose the driver spaces restore each frame, and therefore what the authored angles are composed against. Append-only, same rule as : this is portable preset data, so reordering or deleting a member after presets exist in the wild would silently reinterpret them.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.ClipLayeringGroup.ChannelBlendMode
files.Summary: How one channel's authored angles combine with the base pose. Unobservable while is , because the base is then the rest pose the angles are already measured from. Append-only, same rule as .

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.ClipLayeringGroup
files.Summary: Reserved schema, no consumer. Nothing in this group is read by any code, and its defaults describe exactly what AnyMotion does today. It exists so that the upper-body clip-layering mode — an animation clip supplies the base pose, AnyMotion composes the upper body on top of it — can be added later without a preset-schema break. For the mode itself see Assets/Plan/future/redesign-decision-tree/02-fixed-pose-restore-point/pose-3-real-clip-escape-hatch.md; and locomotion-catalog.md §5 (what this list changes about the P7 schema freeze) for the reservation rule it follows: "an unused field costs nothing, a missing one costs a schema break". P7 (JSON preset schema freeze) is the deadline that makes the reservation worth making now rather than when the mode is built.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.GroundGroup.ContactAnchoring
files.Summary: How a limb's target may move to follow ground it did not author. Reserved 2026-08-02 (roadmap.md §9) as insurance against a P7 schema break; is unimplemented — declaring it now costs nothing, adding it after the freeze would. Append-only: never reorder or delete a member, serialization-format-decision.md §Migration strategy.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.GroundGroup
files.Summary: L05 (foot planting on uneven ground): the authored half of vertical ground conformance. The raycast, height/normal correction and pelvis lowering are runtime behaviour in IkTargetSpaceDriver, not authored data, so they are not here — see roadmap.md §9 and locomotion-catalog.md §3.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.IdleGroup
files.Summary:
L04 (idle): a post-evaluation blend of the walk pose toward standing-neutral, plus breathing and weight-shift added on top. See idle-motion-spec.md.

O12 (start/stop) splits that blend in two. hands the legs to 's decoupled leg cycles — each leg parks and unparks on its own, so a planted foot stays planted while the other leg finishes its step — and leaves the cross-fade owning only what has no leg phase to park: the pelvis, torso, head, arms and the breathing and weight-shift oscillators below. See .

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.LookAtGroup
files.Summary: L01 (look-at / head tracking): the authored half. Adds an additive rotation, in the character's frame, on top of whatever / already produced for this frame — it does not override them. IkTargetSpaceDriver is where the live LookAtTarget Transform is read and turned into a yaw/pitch angle; nothing here needs a world position, so it stays portable like every other group.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.PelvisGroup.GravitySource
files.Summary: L02 (run): where comes from for the flight-phase pelvis arc (GaitMath.FlightHeight). Append-only, same rule as : this is portable preset data, so reordering or deleting a member after presets exist in the wild would silently reinterpret them.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.RunBlendGroup
files.Summary: Walk/run speed blend: the "fully running" endpoint for the handful of fields that actually differ between walking and running (WalkGait.Run()'s own preset note). Ground, Slope, LookAt, Irregularity, Asymmetry and Knees are shared, read unchanged from the rest of regardless of blend weight, so there is exactly one place to keep those in sync rather than two full duplicated presets that could drift apart on settings that have nothing to do with running. WalkGait.StanceFraction is the only accessor that already centralises Duty Factor for every reader (its own doc comment: "never from Parameters directly") — the blend piggybacks on that same accessor, plus private equivalents added in WalkGait.cs for Step Length and Torso Lean. is different in kind from those three: rather than one more individually-overridden target field, it scales several existing Pelvis/Head/Arms amplitudes together, so "more dynamic running" does not need a new override field added here every time another amplitude turns out to want it too — see its own tooltip and WalkGait.EffectiveDynamism.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters.SlopeGroup
files.Summary: L08 (slope adaptation): the authored half. Extends L05 (foot planting on uneven ground) — the ground normals it tilts the pelvis towards and the reach deficit it draws step-shortening from both come from L05's existing raycast, so there is no separate authored slope input; only how much of that already-measured slope shows up in the pelvis and the stride is authored here. The raycast, blend and pelvis-rotation math are runtime behaviour in IkTargetSpaceDriver, not authored data, so they are not here — see roadmap.md §1a.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitParameters
files.Summary: The authored slider set for a walk. This is the portable, rig-independent unit: the same values should produce the same visible walk on a 1.28 m mouse and a 1.87 m Pumpkinhulk.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Gait.WalkGaitPreset
files.Summary: A preset, saved and loaded as a Unity asset.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Samples.PerfCharacterState
files.Summary: Test helper for toggling one character between alive/dead and rendered/hidden states. Assumes the assigned GameObject is the logical character root and searches children.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Samples.PerfStressRunner
files.Summary: Runtime helper for P4: spawns N duplicated characters, toggles systems, and records coarse profiler metrics. Use together with Unity Profiler and an FPS overlay.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Samples.PuppetMasterReflectionBridge
files.Summary: Reflection-only bridge for PuppetMaster-style components. Keeps the sample free of a hard RootMotion/PuppetMaster assembly dependency.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Samples.ThirdPersonCharacterController
files.Summary: Third-person locomotion for the P1 hierarchy spike: a driven by the Input System, moving relative to the Cinemachine camera.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Shake.BoneChannel
files.Summary: One noise-driven bone. A preset is a list of these; an empty list drives nothing.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Shake.BoneNoiseDriver
files.Summary: L37 (shake & noise generator): per-bone rotational tremor, jitter and noise, applied additively on top of whatever pose the rig already has this frame. See shake-noise-spec.md for the design decisions behind this class.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Shake.ShakeEnvelope
files.Summary: Which envelope scales a channel's amplitude. See shake-noise-spec.md §5.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Shake.ShakeNoiseParameters
files.Summary: The authored bone-noise channel list for one . This is the portable unit — every channel drives rotation only, in degrees, so unlike WalkGaitParameters it needs no per-rig normalisation to stay portable across rigs of different size or shape.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Shake.ShakeNoisePreset
files.Summary: A preset, saved and loaded as a Unity asset.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Spaces.BoneFrameSpaceDriver
files.Summary: Space B: writes each bone's rotation directly, with the authored angles expressed in the character's frame rather than in each bone's own local frame.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Spaces.GaitDriverSpaceKind
files.Summary: Which of the three candidate driver spaces of the P2 spike is in use.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Spaces.HumanoidBoneSet
files.Summary: Resolved bone Transforms of one Humanoid rig, plus a snapshot of their bind pose.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Spaces.IGaitDriverSpace
files.Summary: Applies a to a rig. The three implementations exist to be compared: each consumes the same pose from the same parameters, so a difference in the result is attributable to the space and not to different timing or different gait maths.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Spaces.IkTargetSpaceDriver
files.Summary: Space C: places the feet, and optionally the hands, at the positions the gait asked for, using an analytic two-bone IK solve.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.AnimateYourself.Spaces.MuscleSpaceDriver
files.Summary: Space A: writes Mecanim muscle values through HumanPoseHandler.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.Noise.Axis3D
files.Summary: Which local axes a noise or shake channel drives. Combinable, so a channel can drive any subset.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.Noise.NoiseMath
files.Summary: Pure, allocation-free noise and oscillator functions shared by every product. Rig-agnostic: takes and returns plain numbers only, so the same functions can drive a humanoid bone, a camera, or a machine part unmodified. See shake-noise-spec.md §2 and §4 for why this lives in Core and why per-axis 1D noise was chosen over a 3D/vector noise field.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.Noise.Trauma
files.Summary: Squared-decay burst model (Eiserloh's trauma model): a 0..1 value set by an event and decayed back to 0 over time, whose square is used as an amplitude multiplier so a burst starts strong and fades quickly rather than ramping up. Pure functions over plain floats — the caller owns the state, so any driver can add trauma without this type needing to know what a "driver" is.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.Presets.PresetAsset<T>
files.Summary: Wraps one preset data type as a Unity asset. Unity's own asset serialization persists natively; no code here is needed for that. Text-based save/load — sharing a preset outside the project — is a separate concern handled by CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad, not by this class.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.Rig.BindPose
files.Summary: The pose a rig was skinned in, read from the mesh's own bind pose matrices rather than from the rig's current state in the scene.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.Rig.RigMetrics.Metrics
files.Summary: Measured dimensions of one Humanoid rig. All lengths are metres in world scale.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.Rig.RigMetrics
files.Summary: Measures the body dimensions of a Humanoid rig, so that animation parameters (step length, knee height, hip sway) can be authored as fractions of the character's own proportions rather than as absolute metres. One preset then produces the same visible motion on rigs of different sizes.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.DefaultSaveSystem
files.Summary: The default composition: JSON text over plain files. Convenience for the common case; build a directly when a different serializer or file I/O is needed instead.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.IFileIO
files.Summary: Reads and writes preset text at a file path. Knows nothing about JSON or ScriptableObjects, so it can be swapped or mocked independently of both.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.ISaveSystem
files.Summary: Saves and loads preset-shaped data as text. Composes an and an ; knows nothing about PresetAsset<T> or ScriptableObjects, so it is reusable for any serializable data, not only preset assets.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.ITextSerializer
files.Summary: Converts preset data to and from a text representation. Isolated behind an interface so the format can change (eg JSON to a binary format) without touching file I/O or the save system that composes this with it.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.JsonUtilityTextSerializer
files.Summary: The only format in use today. See serialization-format-decision.md for why.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.LoadException
files.Summary: A load operation failed. See for the underlying cause.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.LoadResult<T>
files.Summary: Outcome of a load. Never throws — check instead, per serialization-format-decision.md's "must never fail to load" requirement.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.SaveException
files.Summary: A save operation failed. See for the underlying cause.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.SaveLoadException
files.Summary: Base for every exception wraps an underlying failure in.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.SaveResult
files.Summary: Outcome of a save. Never throws — check instead, per serialization-format-decision.md's "must never fail to load" requirement applied to saving too.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.SaveSystem
files.Summary: Default . Wraps expected I/O and format failures into a Result rather than throwing, so callers never need a try/catch around Save or Load. Exceptions outside that expected set — eg a bug in a custom — still propagate, because those are programming errors, not the external-input failures this exists to handle.

files.Title: CodeSmile.AnyMotion.Core.SaveLoad.SystemFileIO
files.Summary: Plain wrapper. Works in the Editor and in builds.
